To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the chemical composition of the particulate matter is influenced by both the local and the synoptic scale atmospheric circulation, which are responsible for the transport of the air masses and the formation of the particulate material.

the ionic composition of the collected PM10, PM2:5 and PM1 samples is influenced by the meteorological conditions, while the dominant species are the Na+ cations in winter and the SO42- anion in summer.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the chemical characterization of PM10, PM2·5, and PM1 fractions in an urban and a rural site in Athens, during two different seasons, and the influence of meteorological conditions to the chemical composition of the particulate matter.

the characterization of the particulate matter associated to the VOCs in the urban and suburban regions of the Greater Athens area and the identification of the major sources and processes responsible for the formation and transport of particulates in this area.

the chemical characterization of PM10, PM2,5, PM1, and VOCs in the Greater Athens Area, and their association with meteorological and synoptic conditions, in an effort to better understand and evaluate the impact of air pollution in the area.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the meteorological parameters (temperature, wind speed and direction) are the most significant parameters in the distribution of particulate matter and its ionic constituents in the Greater Athens Area, while the chemical characteristics (dominant character) of the particulate matter are mainly influenced by the synoptic scale atmospheric circulation.

the meteorological parameters, such as the air mass origin, the wind speed, the relative humidity, and the temperature, have a significant impact on the concentration of the ionic species and on the particulate size distribution.
, in general, during winter, the acidic character of PM is dominant at both sites, while during summer, the alkaline character of PM is more significant at the urban site.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ionic composition of PM2.1 and PM10 was dominated by the alkaline species, Na+, K+, Mg2+, and Ca2+, and by the acid species, NO3-, Cl-, and SO42- during winter and summer periods, respectively, in the urban site.

the ionic species size distribution in PM2.5 and PM10 fractions is affected significantly from the meteorological parameters, especially from the temperature and relative humidity, while the PM1 fraction seems not to be affected by them.
the ions' species size distribution in PM10, PM2,5 and PM1, as well as the chemical character of the particulates are influenced by the atmospheric circulation and the local emissions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ionic composition of the particulate matter is affected by the atmospheric circulation patterns, which are associated with the local and regional sources.
the ionic composition of PM is a function of the VOCs concentration, the meteorological conditions, the atmospheric circulation and the sampling site.
the ionic composition of particulate matter is highly variable and is influenced by the meteorological conditions.
